name: Faye Wong
description:
'''Faye Wong''' ({{lang-zh|王菲}}; [[pinyin]]: ''Wáng Fēi''; born 8 August 1969) is a [[Hong Kong]] singer-songwriter and actress. Early in her career, she briefly used the [[stage name]] '''Shirley Wong''' ({{lang|zh|王靖雯}}). Born in [[Beijing]], she moved to [[British Hong Kong|Hong Kong]] at the age of 18. Her debut album ''[[Shirley Wong (album)|Shirley Wong]]'' (1989) was in [[Cantonese]] and her breakthrough came with the [[Cantopop]] song "Fragile Woman" in 1992. She established her style by blending [[alternative pop|alternative music]] with [[C-pop|Chinese pop]], and since the late 1990s has recorded primarily in her native [[Standard Chinese|Mandarin]]. In 2000, Wong was recognised by [[Guinness World Records]] as the best selling [[Cantopop]] female artist, having sold an estimated 9.7 million copies of her albums by March 2000. Upon her second marriage in 2005, she withdrew from the limelight and moved back to Beijing, making only occasional stage appearances. In 2009, Wong was voted the second most influential Chinese celebrity of the past 60 years in a poll conducted by the [[State Council Information Office]] to commemorate the 60th anniversary of the [[China|People's Republic of China]]. 

One of the biggest names in the [[Sinophone|Chinese-speaking world]], Wong has also gained followings in [[Japan]] and [[Southeast Asia]]. In the West, she is perhaps best known for starring in [[Wong Kar-wai]]'s films ''[[Chungking Express]]'' (1994) and ''[[2046 (film)|2046]]'' (2004). Often titled "diva" or "heavenly queen" in Chinese, Wong has gained a reputation for her [[Cool (aesthetic)|"cool" personality]]. In ''Encyclopedia of Contemporary Chinese Culture'', Jeroen de Kloet characterised her as "singer, actress, mother, celebrity, royalty, sex symbol and diva all at the same time."
